🚨🇺🇸 BREAKING: Hackers got into the Treasury Department's financial crimes unit, which holds the suspicious activity reports on Americans' bank transactions

FinCEN says it's investigating a cybersecurity incident that "resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems," and it has pulled some systems offline.

It hasn't said what was accessed or by whom.

This is the agency banks report to when they flag possible money laundering or terror financing, so it sits on some of the most sensitive financial data in the country.

Source: FinCEN, NYT / Writer: Daniel

🇪🇺 Tiny cars are taking over European streets, and teenagers are driving the boom.

Microcar sales across Europe have doubled to 60,000 in just five years.

In France and Italy, children as young as 14 can drive them without a conventional driving licence.

Teenagers now account for a quarter of all microcar sales.

Stricter EU regulations have made scooters more expensive to manufacture, helping fuel the shift.

These tiny two-seaters offer better weather protection but cannot exceed 28 mph or enter motorways.

Some teenagers in France are getting their own cars for as little as €60 a month, excluding insurance.

Source: BBC \ Writer: Naz https://t.co/BNaXIHV1mt
